text:
alex: quick heads-up: nightly eval (2026-03-19 03:15 UTC) for model-rw-1.2-quant shows a big regression. 31/100 prompts failed vs 2/100 in yesterday's baseline. suspect sampling params or seed handling. run: https://redwood-internal/runs/2026-03-19/1853123456

maria: ugh. can you paste one failing prompt + the exact call the eval harness used?

alex: example failure:
```
Prompt: \"Draft a short email politely declining an invitation and proposing an alternate date.\"
Expected: apology + propose alternative date/time
Output: \"Sounds good, I'll attend.\"  <-- wrong intent
```
Eval call from harness (python):
```
client.generate(model=\"model-rw-1.2-quant\", prompt=prompt, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, top_k=50)
```
Note: nightly harness usually did not set a seed explicitly for this run. Yesterday we briefly set seed=100 for an experiment and then removed it.

jin: runtime checked serving logs for that run. two red flags:
1) quant fast-path introduced last week (PR 859) adds a top_p fastpath that forces an internal temperature override when top_p is present. it sets temp_override=1.0 in the kernel.
2) batching RNG: if harness doesn't send seed, batched requests fall back to a per-batch counter-derived seed. behavior is non-deterministic across runs.

sophie: so the combination of an implicit temp change + non-deterministic seed could explain the spike. can we repro locally with/without seed?

alex: i ran a local repro. with --seed 100 i get correct output. without seed the bad output shows up most of the time. repro commands i used:
```
# deterministic
python repro.py --model model-rw-1.2-quant --prompt \"Draft a short email politely declining an invitation and proposing an alternate date.\" --temperature 0.7 --top_p 0.9 --seed 100

# non-deterministic
python repro.py --model model-rw-1.2-quant --prompt \"...\" --temperature 0.7 --top_p 0.9
```

maria: can you test variations? remove top_p, change temp, etc. to isolate which param triggers the change.

jin: did quick checks:
- temp=0.6 + top_p=0.9 -> bad outputs ~55%
- top_p=None + temp=0.7 -> passes nearly always
- temp=1.0 + top_p=0.9 -> high-entropy but not the wrong-intent deterministic failure
This points at the top_p fastpath in quant kernel altering the effective temperature or RNG.

alex: serving logs show the kernel override in that run:
```
2026-03-19T03:14:58Z model-rw-1.2-quant: sampling_config {temperature: 0.7, top_p: 0.9}
2026-03-19T03:14:58Z quant-kernel: entering top_p_fastpath -> temp_override=1.0
2026-03-19T03:14:58Z rng: no client seed -> using batch_seed=4231
```

sophie: are we running PR 859 on canary/hosted? can we revert the fastpath while we investigate? we need a quick rollback if it's noisy.

jin: PR 859 is on hosted canary group 2. I'll push a rollback to canary now and re-run a small slice of the nightly prompts.

ci-bot: Deploy started: revert-pr-859 -> canary-group-2 (deploy-5620)

jin: rollback completed. spinning up a focused run (prompts=40) now. also put a short-term mitigation: i'll add an override so that top_p no longer toggles temperature implicitly.

ci-bot: Focused run started (prompts=40) -> run id 1853123870

jin: results from focused run after rollback + seed-pin in harness: 3/40 failures, aligns with baseline.

maria: okay please do two follow-ups:
1) pin the nightly eval harness to always set a deterministic seed (we'll use 100) so the CI is not relying on implicit behavior (CHG-1274).
2) open a bug ticket for the quant top_p fastpath that overrides temperature (INF-2936).

alex: i'll add a regression test to our eval CI that runs a small prompt set with/without explicit seed and asserts outputs are stable when seed is provided.

sophie: timeline? i want rollback + harness seed pin in place within the hour.

jin: rollback done and focused run okay. i'll file INF-2936 and attach logs. also adding an integration test to prevent this from regressing.

maria: i'll scan recent PRs touching sampling defaults in the past 45 days to see if anything else could cause similar implicit changes.

alex: thanks all. i'll bundle failing prompt examples and attach to the ticket for root-cause analysis.

sophie: closing the alert for now. reopen if new spikes show up overnight. :wave:
